proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(\mathcal P\) be an input-free COPAG, let \(A_0,B_0\subseteq V\) be disjoint with \(A_0\neq\varnothing\), and let \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). Suppose \(\operatorname{sIDP}(\mathcal P;A_0,B_0,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) returns a proxy kernel \(H(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\), with a continuous version chosen at every application of Rule L2 as required by Theorem 4.14(3). Then, pointwise on the discrete assignment domain,
\[
 H(P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M})
 =P_{\mathbf M}(A_0\mid\operatorname{do}(B_0),S=\mathbf 1)
\]
for every represented \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\). The restriction to the positive discrete class \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\) is licensed by Remark 4.4(2).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current pointwise claim incorrectly quantifies over all permitted oracle choices. The attested source proves pointwise equality only when continuous versions are chosen at every Rule L2 application; Remark 4.4(2) supplies the positive discrete specialization.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
Fix a terminal role state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) and a displayed finite legal role trace
\[
 \pi:\rho_0=(X,C)\longrightarrow\rho_1\longrightarrow\cdots\longrightarrow\rho_\ell=\rho
\]
in \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\). Let \(a\) be the assignment on \(W=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}C\) determined by \(a_X=x\) and \(a_C=c\), and set \(\bar x=a_{\bar X}\) and \(\bar c=a_{\bar C}\). Fix represented coordinates \(\mathcal M\in[\mathcal P]_{\mathsf M}\) and \(\mathcal G\in[\mathcal M]_{\mathsf G}\), and nested \(R_F\)-rooted forests \(F'\subsetneq F\) satisfying the terminal selected-hedge predicates for the entire terminal intervention \(\bar X\). Choose one normalized local table \(\theta\) of the rational interior base model \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\), choose a rational simplex-tangent direction \(v=R_Tq\), and define \(\mathbf M(t)\) by replacing \(\theta\) with \(\theta+t v\) while holding every other local mechanism fixed. The terminal masses of this family are evaluated at the inherited assignments \((y,\bar c;\bar x)\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former construction did not carry the reachable terminal state, its legal role trace, the inherited assignments, or the requirement that the forest predicates cover the entire terminal intervention. Those data are necessary to transfer terminal numerator disagreement to the original conditional query.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: The map \(\operatorname{LockCompile}\) retains from the supplied affine family its terminal state \(\rho\), displayed legal trace \(\pi\), represented coordinates \(\mathcal M,\mathcal G\), nested forests \(F'\subsetneq F\), common root set \(R_F\), and inherited terminal assignments. It applies rational row reduction to \(E_T\) and \(b_T\). When the augmented-rank test passes, it selects a rational \(q\in\ker(E_T)\) with \(b_Tq\neq0\), sets \(v=R_Tq\), and chooses a nonzero rational \(t\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\) inside the supplied exact positivity radius \(\delta\). It sets \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\), expands their exact rational evaluation tables, and copies \(\rho,\pi,\mathcal M,\mathcal G,F,F'\), and \(R_F\), together with the inherited assignments, tables, and arithmetic trace, into \(\Gamma\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: A checkable locked certificate must serialize the reachable state and trace, represented graph coordinates, complete terminal forests, model pair, and exact evaluations rather than silently importing that scaffold in the theorem proof.

prose_updates.tldr: Branch-sCIDP is a finite sound formula search over the published positive discrete selected-COPAG class, with pointwise terminal soundness conditioned on the continuous-version choices required by Chen--Mooij's Theorem 4.14(3). The reusable selection-equalizer lift constructs denominator-locked selected witnesses from suitable observationally equivalent base SCMs. Separately, the affine compiler is a conditional one-table observational-fiber rank test: for a supplied represented family with an explicit reachable role trace, it simultaneously preserves the normalized selected observational law and the positive conditioning denominator while extracting a rational pair with different joint numerators. The implication from all-branch failure to such a represented locked construction, and therefore the advertised formula-or-certificate complexity theorem, remains open.

project_justification.gap: Failure of a selected terminal joint-identification call does not by itself preserve its conditioning denominator. The published pointwise soundness result also requires continuous versions at Rule L2 applications and does not prove selected conditional completeness, leaving the residual-forest-to-lock implication unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The paper separates a sound reachable-role formula search from two constructive nonidentification tools: a reusable selection-equalizer lift and a conditional exact rank compiler on a supplied one-table observational fiber. The graph-to-lock implication connecting universal branch failure to either tool is retained as an open question.
project_justification.fill: The precise affine addition is simultaneous exact preservation of the complete normalized selected observational law and the terminal conditioning denominator, separation of the terminal joint numerator, and extraction of an explicit positive rational certificate. Its transfer to the original query uses the affine family's displayed legal role trace. The equalizer lift supplies an independent reusable construction, while no general formula-or-certificate synthesis theorem is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: Chen and Mooij provide the selected-COPAG model and pointwise \(\operatorname{sIDP}\) soundness under the continuous-version hypothesis in Theorem 4.14(3), with Remark 4.4(2) covering the positive discrete subclass. Their results motivate the role search and residual-forest question but do not supply denominator-locked selected conditional completeness. Jaber, Ribeiro, Zhang, and Bareinboim's Algorithm 2 supplies the no-selection CIDP bucket-intersection transitions and normalization, and their Theorem 4 supplies completeness; the present regression claim is limited to equality of identification decisions. Abouei and coauthors address an unconditional selected intervention target in a known augmented graph. Shpitser and Pearl give the fixed-graph conditional benchmark, and Duarte and coauthors motivate exact finite discrete fiber computation. Against this background, the equalizer lift is used as a reusable construction lemma, whereas the affine compiler is a conditional exact rank test for simultaneous observational-law and denominator preservation on a supplied one-table family, with rational certificate extraction.
prose_updates.honest_scope: No selected conditional completeness theorem is claimed. Pointwise use of \(\operatorname{sIDP}\) is restricted to runs choosing continuous versions at every Rule L2 application. The no-selection comparison asserts equality of identification decisions only; it neither asserts equality of returned functionals nor imports an unattested CIDP soundness theorem. The affine rank equivalence applies to a supplied rational interior one-table family that includes a reachable terminal state, a displayed legal trace, inherited assignments, represented graph coordinates, forests for the entire terminal intervention, and an interval remaining in the represented model class. The compiler's guarantee is simultaneous exact preservation of the normalized selected observational law and the positive conditioning denominator with separation of the numerator and rational certificate extraction. The generic equalizer lift produces a positive rational finite witness in the published discrete class and is binary only when all endogenous and latent base variables are binary; the explicit table and affine certificates are binary. An isolated conditioning root makes denominator equality vacuous, so the deleted bow baseline is not evidence for graph-to-lock. Universal all-branch failure has not been shown to yield a passing represented family, and no \(O(3^n\operatorname{poly}(n)+L_{\Gamma})\) formula-or-certificate synthesis theorem is asserted. Continuous variables, intervention inputs, faithfulness-only conclusions, and general finite-alphabet certificate completeness remain outside scope.

proofs.proof_tex:
Work with the post-change construction in \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family}.  Thus the supplied data include a terminal state \(\rho=(\bar X,\bar C)\), a displayed trace
\[
 \pi:\rho_0=(X,C)\longrightarrow\rho_1\longrightarrow\cdots
 \longrightarrow\rho_m=\rho                                      \tag{1}
\]
in \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\), the restrictions of the assignment \((x,c)\) at every state, represented graphs \(\mathcal M,\mathcal G\), and nested forests satisfying the terminal selected-hedge predicates for the entire intervention \(\bar X\).  No role-trace datum will be inferred from a forest.  The algebraic part of the proof uses only the supplied affine family; the transfer to \(\psi\) will use exactly (1).

By \texttt{def:rational-binary-class}, \texttt{ass:binary-certificate-support}, and \texttt{ass:rational-interior-mechanisms}, the base model \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) has finite binary state spaces and rational local stochastic-mechanism entries in \((0,1)\).  Fix either the observational regime or the terminal regime \(\operatorname{do}(\bar X=\bar x)\), and fix a complete assignment \(\omega\) of its nonintervened endogenous and latent variables.  Its truncated factorization contains the varied local table at most once.  If that factor is retained and its coordinate at \(\omega\) is \(j(\omega)\), then
\[
 p_t(\omega)
 =\bigl(\theta_{j(\omega)}+t v_{j(\omega)}\bigr)
   \prod_{\ell\ne j(\omega)}p_\ell(\omega)
 =p_0(\omega)+t\dot p_v(\omega).                              \tag{2}
\]
If the governed variable is intervened upon, truncation removes that factor and \(p_t(\omega)=p_0(\omega)\).  The full assignment spaces are finite, so marginalizing (2) gives rational linear forms in \(v\), denoted by dots, for which
\[
\begin{aligned}
 o_z(t)&=o_z(0)+t\dot o_z(v),&
 Z_o(t)&=Z_o(0)+t\dot Z_o(v),\\
 h(t)&=h(0)+t\dot h(v),&
 k(t)&=k(0)+t\dot k(v),&
 Z_x(t)&=Z_x(0)+t\dot Z_x(v).
\end{aligned}                                                   \tag{3}
\]
Thus these identities are exact for finite \(t\), rather than first-order approximations.

At \(t=0\), strict positivity of every local factor implies strict positivity of every complete-assignment mass compatible with an intervention.  Since \(S=\mathbf 1\) and the assigned value \(\bar C=\bar c\) are in their binary supports, the relevant finite sums satisfy
\[
 Z_o(0)>0,\qquad Z_x(0)>0,qquad h(0)>0.                       \tag{4}
\]
The same statements hold at every perturbation for which all local entries remain strictly positive.  By the definitions of \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), \(D_\rho\), and \(N_\rho\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M(t)}(z)=\frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)},\qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}(\bar c;\bar x)=\frac{h(t)}{Z_x(t)},
 \qquad
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}(y,\bar c;\bar x)=\frac{k(t)}{Z_x(t)}. \tag{5}
\]
Substitution of (3) into (5), followed by exact cross-multiplication, yields
\[
 \frac{o_z(t)}{Z_o(t)}-\frac{o_z(0)}{Z_o(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_o(0)\dot o_z(v)-o_z(0)\dot Z_o(v)\}}
        {Z_o(t)Z_o(0)},                                        \tag{6}
\]
\[
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-D_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot h(v)-h(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)},                                        \tag{7}
\]
and
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M(t)}-N_{\rho,\mathbf M(0)}
 =\frac{t\{Z_x(0)\dot k(v)-k(0)\dot Z_x(v)\}}
        {Z_x(t)Z_x(0)}.                                        \tag{8}
\]
The products of the two slopes cancel in each numerator.  Consequently (6)--(8) are exact identities for every admissible \(t\).  By \texttt{def:affine-rank-system}, after writing \(v=R_Tq\), the braces in all instances of (6), followed by the brace in (7), are the coordinates of \(E_Tq\), while the brace in (8) is \(b_Tq\).

We next establish the rank criterion over \(\mathbb Q\).  If \(b_T\) belongs to the row space of \(E_T\), then \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  Conversely, suppose that \(b_Tq=0\) for every \(q\in\ker(E_T)\).  The prescription
\[
 \ell(E_Tq)=b_Tq                                                \tag{9}
\]
is then a well-defined rational linear functional on \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\), because two preimages differ by an element of \(\ker(E_T)\).  Extend a rational basis of \(\operatorname{im}(E_T)\) to one of its codomain and extend \(\ell\) arbitrarily on the added basis vectors.  Equation (9) then gives \(b_T=\ell E_T\), so \(b_T\) lies in the row space of \(E_T\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\exists q\in\mathbb Q^{\dim(T)}:\ E_Tq=0\ \text{and}\ b_Tq\ne0\\
 &\quad\Longleftrightarrow b_T\notin\operatorname{row}(E_T)
 \Longleftrightarrow
 \operatorname{rank}\!\begin{bmatrix}E_T\\ b_T\end{bmatrix}
 >\operatorname{rank}(E_T).                                    \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
Exact rational row reduction decides (10) and, in the strict-rank case, returns a rational null vector \(q\) with \(b_Tq\ne0\).

Let \(R_T'\) be another rational basis matrix for \(T\).  There is an invertible rational matrix \(H\) such that \(R_T'=R_TH\).  Therefore
\[
 ER_T'=E_TH,qquad bR_T'=b_TH.                                  \tag{11}
\]
Right multiplication by \(H\) preserves each rank in (10).  Moreover, \(q'=H^{-1}q\) represents the same mechanism direction, since \(R_T'q'=R_Tq\).  This proves basis independence.

Assume (10), take the returned \(q\), and put \(v=R_Tq\).  Since \(b_Tq=bv\ne0\), one has \(v\ne0\).  Define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{pos}}
 =\frac12\min_{j:v_j\ne0}
 \left\{\frac{\theta_j}{|v_j|},
              \frac{1-\theta_j}{|v_j|}\right\}.               \tag{12}
\]
This is a positive rational number.  Membership \(v\in T\) says that the coordinates of \(v\) sum to zero in every probability block.  Hence \(\theta+t v\) stays normalized, and (12) gives \(0<\theta_j+t v_j<1\) for every coordinate whenever \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{pos}}\).

We also check represented-class membership.  The corrected affine-family construction fixes the state spaces, parent indexing, directed and latent incidences, selection vertices, and all unvaried local tables.  Thus no perturbation can create an incidence not displayed by \(\mathcal G\).  If representation permits displayed incidences with inactive numerical effects, this already proves compatibility for every positive perturbation.  Under the minimal active-incidence convention, let \(\mathcal A\) be the finite set of displayed incidences whose activity is witnessed in the varied table.  Because \(\mathbf M_{\mathrm{base}}\) realizes \(\mathcal G\), for every \(a\in\mathcal A\) there are two coordinates \(j_a,j_a'\), differing only in the argument indexed by that incidence, such that
\[
 \alpha_a=\theta_{j_a}-\theta_{j_a'}\ne0.                     \tag{13}
\]
Put \(\beta_a=v_{j_a}-v_{j_a'}\) and define
\[
 \delta_{\mathrm{rep}}
 =\begin{cases}
 1,&\text{if }\beta_a=0\text{ for all }a\in\mathcal A,\\[1mm]
 \displaystyle\min\!\left\{1,
   \frac12\min_{a:\beta_a\ne0}\frac{|\alpha_a|}{|\beta_a|}\right\},
 &\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}                                                    \tag{14}
\]
This number is positive and rational.  If \(|t|<\delta_{\mathrm{rep}}\), then for every \(a\) with \(\beta_a\ne0\),
\[
 |\alpha_a+t\beta_a|
 \ge |\alpha_a|-|t|\,|\beta_a|
 >\frac12|\alpha_a|>0,                                        \tag{15}
\]
while a contrast with \(\beta_a=0\) is unchanged.  Thus every required active incidence remains active.  All other structural and latent incidences were fixed by construction, so the same represented realization is retained.

Set
\[
 \delta=\min\{\delta_{\mathrm{pos}},\delta_{\mathrm{rep}}\}. \tag{16}
\]
Equations (12)--(16) make \(\delta\in\mathbb Q_{>0}\) exactly computable.  For each rational \(t\) with \(0<|t|<\delta\), all changed entries are rational, normalized, and strictly positive, and the binary state spaces and represented realization are unchanged.  Therefore, with \(\mathbf M_0=\mathbf M(0)\) and \(\mathbf M_1=\mathbf M(t)\),
\[
 \mathbf M_0,\mathbf M_1
 \in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{rat,bin}}^+(\mathcal P)
 \subseteq\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P).                         \tag{17}
\]

All denominators in (6)--(8) are positive by (4), (12), and (17).  Since \(E_Tq=0\), equations (6)--(7) give, for every full observed cell \(z\),
\[
 P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_0}(z)=P_{\mathrm{obs},\mathbf M_1}(z),
 \qquad
 D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(\bar c;\bar x)
 =D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(\bar c;\bar x)>0.                     \tag{18}
\]
Thus the normalized selected observational law and the selected terminal denominator are both preserved exactly.  Since \(b_Tq\ne0\) and \(t\ne0\), equation (8) gives
\[
 N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(y,\bar c;\bar x)
 \ne N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(y,\bar c;\bar x).                 \tag{19}
\]
Combining the common positive denominator in (18) with (19) yields
\[
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_0}(\bar c;\bar x)}
 \ne
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_1}(\bar c;\bar x)}.                 \tag{20}
\]

We now use the explicit trace (1), which is the stated condition for transferring (20) to the original query.  Write \(\rho_i=(\bar X_i,\bar C_i)\).  If the edge from \(\rho_i\) to \(\rho_{i+1}\) moves a nonempty set \(B_i\) from intervention to conditioning, then
\[
 \bar X_i=B_i\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar X_{i+1},
 \qquad
 \bar C_{i+1}=B_i\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C_i.                \tag{21}
\]
Apply \texttt{lem:selected-rule-two} with \(A_0=Y\), \(B_0=B_i\), \(C_0=\bar C_i\), and \(D_0=\bar X_{i+1}\).  These four sets are pairwise disjoint because each role state partitions \(W=X\mathbin{\dot\cup}C\) and \texttt{ass:disjoint-query-sets} gives \(Y\cap W=\varnothing\).  The required Rule--2 separation is exactly the legality label of the edge in (1), and its positive-assignment premise follows from (17).  Using the inherited value restrictions specified in \texttt{def:affine-mechanism-family}, the lemma gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &P_{\mathbf M_j}\!\left(Y=y\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\bar X_i=\bar x_i),
       \bar C_i=\bar c_i,S=\mathbf1\right)\\
 &\quad=P_{\mathbf M_j}\!\left(Y=y\mid
       \operatorname{do}(\bar X_{i+1}=\bar x_{i+1}),
       \bar C_{i+1}=\bar c_{i+1},S=\mathbf1\right),
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.                                         \tag{22}
 \end{aligned}
\]
A reverse move is the same equality read from right to left.  Induction over the finite displayed trace, and then the definitions of \(D_\rho\), \(N_\rho\), and \(\psi\), give
\[
 \frac{N_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(y,\bar c;\bar x)}
      {D_{\rho,\mathbf M_j}(\bar c;\bar x)}
 =P_{\mathbf M_j}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c,S=\mathbf1)
 =\psi_{\mathbf M_j}(y;x,c),
 \qquad j\in\{0,1\}.                                         \tag{23}
\]
Equations (18), (20), and (23) exhibit two members of the published class with the same \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) but different \(\psi\).  By \texttt{def:identification}, this proves nonidentification over \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  This is only the valid negative transfer from the subclass inclusion in (17); it asserts no positive completeness transfer.  The post-change \texttt{def:lock-compiler} copies \(\rho\), the actual trace (1), its assignment restrictions, the represented graph data, and the forests for the entire terminal intervention into \(\Gamma\).  Together with (17)--(19) and the expanded exact tables, these are precisely the certificate data in \texttt{def:locked-certificate}.

It remains to prove the bit-complexity assertions.  Clear the encoded rational denominators of \(E_T\) and \(b_T\), and perform pivoted fraction-free elimination.  With a nonzero pivot, an uneliminated entry is updated by
\[
 a_{ij}^{(r+1)}
 =\frac{a_{rr}^{(r)}a_{ij}^{(r)}-a_{ir}^{(r)}a_{rj}^{(r)}}
        {a_{r-1,r-1}^{(r-1)}},                                 \tag{24}
\]
where the initial previous pivot is one; row and column permutations provide a nonzero pivot whenever one exists.  Expanding the determinants in (24) around the pivot shows inductively that the division is exact and that each stored nonzero integer is, up to sign, a minor of the integerized input.  If the matrix dimensions are at most \(s\) and its entries have bit length at most \(B\), the Leibniz formula bounds an \(r\)-by-\(r\) minor by \(r!2^{rB}\), and hence bounds its bit length by
\[
 rB+\lceil\log_2(r!)\rceil+1
 =O\!\left(s(B+\log s)\right).                               \tag{25}
\]
There are polynomially many updates, and (25) bounds all intermediate bit lengths polynomially in the encoded matrix length.  Back-substitution performs polynomially many rational operations at those bit lengths and returns \(q\).  Scanning the finite varied table finds the activity witnesses in (13), after which (12), (14), (16), and a choice such as \(t=\delta/2\) use polynomially many exact rational operations.  Thus the ranks, \(q\), \(v\), \(\delta\), and \(t\) are computed in \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}})\) bit operations.

The compiler copies the already supplied finite graph, trace, assignment, and forest data, and expands the two model evaluations.  Every complete-assignment atom is a finite product of encoded rational local entries, and every reported marginal is a finite exact sum of such atoms.  The dense atoms and arithmetic trace are part of the output measured by \(L_\Gamma\); sequential multiplication and addition have operand lengths polynomial in the total input-plus-output length.  Construction and writing therefore take \(\operatorname{poly}(L_{\mathrm{temp}}+L_\Gamma)\) bit operations.

Finally, the verifier checks endpoint compatibility, acyclicity, ancestry, the displayed latent projection, legality of every edge of \(\pi\), and the nested rooted-forest predicates by adjacency scans, separation tests, and directed-reachability searches on the displayed graphs. \[

proofs.proof_tex:
Assume \(S=\varnothing\).  Since the selection event is then certain, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}target\text{-}query}\) gives
\[
 \psi_{\mathbf M}(y;x,c)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x),C=c).
 \tag{1}
\]
The conditioning stratum in (1) is positive by \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}discrete\text{-}selected\text{-}model}\), as incorporated into that definition.

First suppose that Branch-sCIDP returns a formula.  By Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}branch\text{-}soundness}\), that formula equals (1) for every model \(\mathbf M\in\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).  Thus the conditional effect in (1) is identified from the represented observational law.  The completeness direction in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\) says that CIDP cannot return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\) for an identifiable conditional effect.  Hence CIDP returns a formula.

Conversely, suppose that CIDP returns a formula.  By the transition contract in Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}cidp\text{-}no\text{-}selection\text{-}contract}\), its successful execution produces a sequence
\[
 (X,C)=\rho_0\longrightarrow\rho_1\longrightarrow\cdots
 \longrightarrow\rho_k=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star),
 \tag{2}
\]
where every arrow moves a nonempty intersection of a current role set with a bucket and is taken only after the corresponding PAG Rule--2 separation test succeeds.  These are exactly the edge predicates in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\).  Consequently
\[
 \rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)
 \in\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C).
 \tag{3}
\]
The same cited contract says that the final marginal call succeeds with an observed-law expression \(E\) for
\[
 Q_{\rho_\star}
 :=P_{\mathbf M}(Y,\bar C_\star
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star)).
 \tag{4}
\]
Thus (4) is identified on the represented PAG model class and, in particular, on its positive discrete subclass \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\).

The hypotheses of Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}completeness}\) apply to the terminal joint query with
\[
 A_0=Y\cup\bar C_\star,
 \qquad B_0=\bar X_\star.
\]
Indeed, \(A_0\neq\varnothing\) by \(\mathrm{ass{:}nonempty\text{-}outcome}\).  Moreover, \(A_0\cap B_0=\varnothing\): Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}reachable\text{-}role\text{-}graph}\) keeps \(\bar X_\star\mathbin{\dot\cup}\bar C_\star=X\cup C\), while \(\mathrm{ass{:}disjoint\text{-}query\text{-}sets}\) gives \(Y\cap(X\cup C)=\varnothing\).  If the sIDP call at \(\rho_\star\) returned \(\operatorname{Fail}\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}sidp\text{-}completeness}\) would say that (4) is not identified over \(\mathfrak M_d^+(\mathcal P)\), contradicting the preceding paragraph.  Hence that sIDP call succeeds.

By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}branch\text{-}scidp}\), Branch-sCIDP enumerates every state in \(\Omega(\mathcal P;Y,X,C)\) and calls sIDP at each state.  In view of (3), it therefore succeeds either before reaching \(\rho_\star\) or at \(\rho_\star\).  The normalization at the latter state is defined: positivity gives
\[
 \sum_{y'}E(y',\bar c_\star;\bar x_\star)
 =P_{\mathbf M}(\bar C_\star=\bar c_\star
       \mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star=\bar x_\star))>0.
\]
The sum is over the discrete outcome support; if that support is countably infinite, the equality is countable additivity of nonnegative point masses.  When \(\bar C_\star=\varnothing\), the same sum equals one.  We have proved both implications between the two success decisions, which is the claimed equivalence.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: When \(S=\varnothing\), Algorithm~2 CIDP exchanges only nonempty intersections of the current intervention or conditioning set with a bucket, and performs each exchange only after the corresponding displayed PAG Rule--2 separation test succeeds.  On success it reaches a role state \(\rho_\star=(\bar X_\star,\bar C_\star)\), its final marginal-algorithm call returns an observed-law expression for \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y,\bar C_\star\mid\operatorname{do}(\bar X_\star))\), and CIDP divides that expression by its sum over the full discrete support of \(Y\).  Theorem~4 states the completeness direction for identification of \(P_{\mathbf M}(Y\mid\operatorname{do}(X),C)\) from an input-free PAG: if this conditional effect is identifiable, CIDP does not return \(\operatorname{FAIL}\).
